### Original software

serato dj pro

### What the software does

It's DJ software that also has video DJing and an effects suite, but they're all separated into their own convoluted plugins, patches, and extensions, so you have to pay for each layer. Even though I have Pro, which comes with my controller, I don't have all of the effects or the ability to use some of the buttons and knobs that come on the controller (because of the newer updates and the requirement to be on the Pro version, like the paid Pro version, with extra plugins to be able to use the thing). The controller is almost 10 years old, and I can't use it on any other software. The screens only work when they speak with Strato DJ.

### Reason

The software is for running and controlling a lot of different DJ controllers, but specifically, a lot of the Numark DJ controllers are stuck where you can't run any other software unless you want to give up being able to use your displays or the jog wheels (or doing a whole lot of mucking around trying to map the mids). Even then, you don't have some of the functionality because they're sent under specific proprietary protocols, etc.  
  
Just a jailbroken Serato that had a proper wizard to configure any controller and to be able to output MIDI signals as well (with your lights and displays), and just a simple wizard to be able to configure it, would be beautiful.

### Official software URL

_No response_

issues.submission:
### Original software

Chief Architect Premier X18

### What the software does

Chief Architect Premier X18 is a professional residential architectural CAD/BIM application used to design homes, renovations, additions, interiors, and construction documents.

Unlike conventional CAD applications, Chief Architect uses intelligent, parametric building objects. Walls, doors, windows, roofs, floors, foundations, stairs, and framing elements understand their relationships and automatically generate coordinated 2D drawings and 3D building geometry.

### Core capabilities to reimplement

**1. Intelligent 2D/3D architectural modeling**
- Parametric walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, and building assemblies.
- Automatically synchronized 2D floor plans and editable 3D building models.
- Multiple floors, split levels, room definitions, and building elevations.
- Automatic wall intersections, openings, and geometric cleanup.
- Accurate dimensions, snapping, alignment, and CAD editing.
- Real-world units, materials, assembly thicknesses, and construction layers.

**2. Automatic and manual roof design**
- Automatic roof generation based on building geometry.
- Hip, gable, shed, gambrel, mansard, and complex roof configurations.
- Editable roof planes, ridges, valleys, dormers, overhangs, fascia, and soffits.
- Custom pitches, roof heights, framing, and intersections.

**3. Structural modeling and construction documentation**
- Foundations, slabs, footings, floor systems, and framing.
- Automatic wall, floor, ceiling, and roof framing.
- Architectural elevations, cross sections, and construction details.
- Layout sheets, title blocks, schedules, and annotations.
- Door, window, cabinet, and material schedules.
- Material quantities and construction takeoffs.

**4. Interior design and architectural libraries**
- Parametric cabinetry, countertops, fixtures, appliances, and furnishings.
- Kitchens, bathrooms, stairs, railings, and custom millwork.
- Material libraries and surface finishes.
- Manufacturer catalogs and reusable architectural components.

**5. Site modeling and visualization**
- Terrain, elevation data, landscaping, and site plans.
- Exterior and interior 3D camera views.
- Physically based materials, lighting, shadows, and reflections.
- High-quality rendering and walkthroughs.
- Import/export workflows for common CAD and 3D formats.

**6. Professional project workflows**
- Coordinated construction drawings.
- Reusable project templates.
- Accurate geometric measurements and dimensioning.
- Editable architectural assemblies.
- Multiple camera, section, elevation, and plan views.
- Printing, PDF output, and CAD interoperability.

### Essential requirement: AI-ready architectural architecture

The proposed reimplementation should also be designed from the beginning around a documented, programmatically accessible architectural object model.

Rather than treating automation as a later plugin, the application should expose its core modeling operations through a stable API that can be used by scripts, external applications, and AI coding agents.

This would enable direct architectural modeling and automation without requiring agents to simulate mouse clicks.

The goal is a faithful, independently developed implementation of Chief Architect's professional residential design workflows, with a modern, extensible foundation for future AI-assisted design.

### Reason

I am requesting an independent, open-source reimplementation of Chief Architect Premier X18 that preserves its powerful residential architectural design workflows while introducing a modern, automation-first software architecture.

Existing open-source CAD and 3D modeling applications do not provide the same integrated combination of intelligent residential building objects, automatic roof generation, synchronized 2D/3D modeling, and construction documentation in a single purpose-built workflow.

A faithful reimplementation would be valuable on its own. However, the opportunity to introduce native AI and programmatic architectural control makes this project significantly more compelling.

### 1. Native MCP server and AI agent integration — core requirement

The application should include a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, or a first-party MCP adapter backed by the same documented application API.

This would allow tools such as OpenAI Codex and other compatible AI agents to inspect, create, modify, and validate architectural models directly.

Desired capabilities include:

- Create, inspect, update, and delete architectural objects.
- Generate floor plans and building geometry programmatically.
- Place walls, doors, windows, stairs, and structural elements.
- Generate and modify roof systems.
- Access dimensions, coordinates, levels, materials, and construction assemblies.
- Retrieve project metadata and object relationships.
- Generate sections, elevations, schedules, and construction drawings.
- Inspect and correct model errors.
- Export drawings, geometry, schedules, and material quantities.
- Execute multi-step architectural workflows using structured commands.

The MCP integration should operate on actual model data rather than relying on screenshots, mouse automation, or simulated keyboard input.

### 2. Full scripting and automation API

A documented API should expose the application's architectural object model and editing operations.

Preferred capabilities:

- Python scripting support.
- Structured JSON-based commands.
- Local automation endpoints.
- Plugin and extension development.
- Event notifications when project objects change.
- Batch editing and model generation.
- Transactional operations with undo/redo.
- Schema validation and structured error reporting.

The same underlying modeling engine should serve the graphical interface, scripting API, and MCP integration.

This is important because AI automation must not become a separate, less capable modeling system.

### 3. Bidirectional AI and user interaction

AI agents should be able to work directly alongside a human designer.

Example workflow:

1. The user creates an initial residential floor plan.
2. Codex inspects the building model through MCP.
3. The user requests a change, such as enlarging a kitchen or modifying the roof pitch.
4. Codex identifies the affected architectural objects.
5. The application updates the actual parametric building model.
6. The 2D plans, 3D model, and dependent drawings regenerate.
7. The user reviews the modifications and can undo or refine them.

AI-generated changes should be previewable, reversible, and subject to user approval when appropriate.

### 4. AI-assisted drawing interpretation and model reconstruction

A particularly valuable capability would be importing existing architectural drawings and reconstructing editable building models.

Potential inputs include:

- Architectural PDF drawing sets.
- Scanned floor plans.
- CAD drawings.
- Building elevations.
- Sections and construction details.

An AI-assisted workflow could identify walls, openings, dimensions, room boundaries, roof geometry, and other building components.

The system should distinguish verified dimensions from inferred geometry and require confirmation where information is ambiguous.

The output should be editable native architectural objects, not merely a traced image or unstructured 3D mesh.

### 5. Chief Architect X15 and legacy project compatibility

Compatibility with older Chief Architect projects would be highly valuable.

Desired capabilities include:

- Investigating import support for existing Chief Architect X15 `.plan` files.
- Preserving wall geometry, dimensions, openings, levels, materials, and building relationships where possible.
- Investigating `.layout` document interoperability.
- Providing migration reports that identify unsupported or lost information.
- Supporting common interchange formats as alternative migration paths.

Native Chief Architect file formats are proprietary, so full compatibility cannot be assumed. This should be treated as a dedicated technical investigation, using lawful interoperability techniques.

The application should not depend on proprietary Chief Architect source code or licensed assets.

### 6. Modern desktop application

The application should provide a polished, high-performance desktop interface with support for:

- macOS, including Apple Silicon.
- Windows.
- Linux, if practical.
- Hardware-accelerated 2D and 3D viewports.
- Dockable panels and customizable workspaces.
- Professional drafting tools and keyboard shortcuts.
- Modern dark and light interface themes.
- Large architectural models and complex residential projects.

The interface should prioritize professional architectural production rather than a simplified consumer floor-plan editor.

### 7. Extensible rendering and external integrations

The architecture should allow future integration with:

- Blender and other 3D applications.
- External rendering engines.
- PBR material libraries.
- GIS and terrain data.
- Aerial imagery and mapping services.
- Construction estimating systems.
- Quantity takeoff software.
- AI image and visualization services.

These integrations should use documented APIs and interchangeable data formats rather than tightly coupling the application to one provider.

### 8. Suggested technical architecture

A modular implementation would be preferable, separating:

**Architectural model engine**
- Parametric building objects.
- Geometry and topology.
- Constraints and relationships.
- Units, dimensions, and construction assemblies.

**Document and dependency engine**
- Coordinated 2D/3D views.
- Automatic regeneration.
- Sections, elevations, schedules, and layouts.

**Rendering and viewport engine**
- Hardware-accelerated interactive 3D.
- 2D CAD visualization.
- Materials, lighting, and camera systems.

**Automation layer**
- Public application API.
- Python scripting.
- Native MCP integration.
- Plugin system.
- Structured model inspection and editing.

**File interoperability**
- Open native project format.
- CAD and 3D interchange.
- Legacy project migration.
- Import/export validation.

### 9. Suggested development phases

**Phase 1 — Architectural foundation**

Build the parametric architectural object model, intelligent walls, doors, windows, floors, dimensions, and synchronized 2D/3D views.

Establish the scripting API and core automation interfaces during this phase.

**Phase 2 — Building generation**

Implement automatic roof generation, foundations, structural framing, stairs, and advanced building geometry.

**Phase 3 — Professional documentation**

Add construction drawings, elevations, sections, layout sheets, schedules, material quantities, and CAD interoperability.

**Phase 4 — Native AI integration**

Expand the foundational automation API into a complete MCP toolset, supporting Codex-driven architectural modeling, inspection, modification, and validation.

**Phase 5 — Advanced design and visualization**

Add cabinetry, architectural libraries, terrain, materials, lighting, rendering, and external integrations.

**Phase 6 — Legacy interoperability and intelligent workflows**

Investigate Chief Architect X15/X18 project migration, AI-assisted drawing reconstruction, and automated architectural production workflows.

### 10. What would make this project successful?

The objective is not simply a Chief Architect-inspired interface or basic 3D house designer.

A successful reimplementation should demonstrate:

- Intelligent parametric architectural objects.
- Accurate synchronized 2D and 3D modeling.
- Automatic roof generation.
- Professional construction documentation.
- Reliable, editable architectural project files.
- Direct programmatic control over building geometry.
- Native integration with AI coding agents through MCP.
- Human review, undo, and validation of automated changes.
- An extensible architecture that does not require GUI automation for core modeling operations.

The ultimate goal is an independently developed, professional-grade residential CAD/BIM platform that reproduces the most valuable capabilities of Chief Architect Premier X18 while making architectural design fully accessible to modern scripting, automation, and AI agents.

This is a substantial engineering project, so a phased, technically credible implementation would be preferable to an incomplete feature-for-feature clone.

### Official software URL

https://www.chiefarchitect.com/

### Original software

Bluebeam Revu

### What the software does

Bluebeam Revu is a professional PDF editing, markup, measurement, document management, and construction quantity takeoff application widely used by architects, engineers, contractors, estimators, and construction professionals.

Unlike conventional PDF editors, Bluebeam is specifically designed for working with complex architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and civil engineering drawings.

Its defining capabilities include highly accurate drawing measurements, customizable markups, reusable tool sets, document comparison, quantity calculations, and collaborative construction document review.

The requested project is an independent, open-source reimplementation of Bluebeam Revu's major professional workflows, with additional native AI, automated estimating, and direct programmatic control.

### 1. Professional PDF viewing and document management

- Open and render large, multi-page construction PDF sets.
- High-performance zooming, panning, and page navigation.
- Vector and raster PDF support.
- Preserve drawing scale, layers, annotations, and embedded text.
- Page thumbnails, bookmarks, hyperlinks, and drawing indexes.
- Multiple documents and split-screen viewing.
- Searchable drawing text and annotations.
- OCR for scanned construction documents.
- PDF merging, splitting, extracting, rotating, and organizing.
- Batch document processing.
- Drawing revision management.
- Overlay and comparison of drawing revisions.
- Document hyperlinks and cross-references.
- PDF printing and export.

### 2. Professional markup and annotation tools

- Text boxes, callouts, clouds, arrows, lines, shapes, and highlights.
- Custom symbols, stamps, and annotation styles.
- Freehand drawing and sketching.
- Revision clouds and drawing comments.
- Reusable markup tool libraries.
- Custom tool sets for different construction trades.
- Markup grouping, locking, layering, and visibility.
- Markup author, date, status, and category tracking.
- Hyperlinked markups.
- Measurement-based markups.
- Markup filtering, sorting, and searching.
- Import and export of annotations and markup data.

### 3. Accurate construction measurement tools

The measurement engine is one of the most important features to reproduce.

Required capabilities:

- Calibrated drawing scales.
- Imperial and metric measurements.
- Independent scale calibration per page and viewport.
- Length and linear measurements.
- Polyline and perimeter measurements.
- Area and volume measurements.
- Count measurements.
- Angle and radius measurements.
- Arc and curved geometry measurements.
- Polygonal area calculations.
- Multiple measurement units.
- Measurement precision settings.
- Custom measurement formulas.
- Measurement annotations.
- Scale verification and calibration checks.
- Support for drawings containing multiple scales.

Measurements must be based on actual PDF geometry and calibrated drawing coordinates, not estimated visually by AI.

### 4. Construction quantity takeoffs

- Manual and semi-automated quantity measurements.
- Count takeoffs for doors, windows, fixtures, and equipment.
- Linear takeoffs for walls, piping, conduit, framing, and trim.
- Area takeoffs for flooring, roofing, ceilings, drywall, and finishes.
- Volume takeoffs for concrete, excavation, and other materials.
- Reusable takeoff assemblies.
- Quantity grouping by trade, floor, room, or construction phase.
- Measurement labels and categories.
- Automatic quantity totals.
- Material and labour calculation fields.
- Waste factors and adjustment percentages.
- Exportable quantity summaries.
- Spreadsheet and estimating software integration.

### 5. Markup and quantity data management

- A structured markup database.
- Sortable and filterable markup lists.
- Custom data columns.
- Quantity and cost calculations.
- Measurement formulas.
- Trade and classification tags.
- Material and assembly assignments.
- Status and review tracking.
- CSV and Excel export.
- PDF quantity reports.
- Saved markup and takeoff templates.
- Audit history and change tracking.

### 6. Drawing comparison and revision management

- Compare two versions of a construction drawing.
- Overlay drawings with configurable colours and transparency.
- Align drawings using reference points.
- Identify additions, removals, and modifications.
- Highlight revised areas.
- Compare vector and raster drawings.
- Detect changed dimensions and annotations.
- Link revision findings to markups.
- Maintain drawing revision history.
- Generate change reports.

### 7. Construction document collaboration

- Shared markup workflows.
- Review comments and replies.
- Annotation ownership.
- Document status tracking.
- Review and approval workflows.
- Shared project folders.
- Real-time or asynchronous collaboration.
- Role-based permissions.
- Version history.
- Exportable review records.

### 8. Batch automation and document processing

- Batch PDF stamping.
- Batch hyperlinks.
- Batch page labeling.
- Batch drawing comparison.
- Batch quantity extraction.
- Batch annotation processing.
- Automated document naming.
- Drawing sheet indexing.
- Template-based PDF generation.
- Automated reporting.

### 9. Professional desktop application

The requested application should support:

- macOS, including Apple Silicon.
- Windows.
- Linux, where practical.
- Large, multi-monitor workspaces.
- Hardware-accelerated PDF rendering.
- Customizable toolbars and keyboard shortcuts.
- Dockable panels.
- Professional dark and light themes.
- Offline document processing.
- Large construction drawing sets.

The primary goal is to faithfully recreate Bluebeam Revu's professional PDF, markup, measurement, and quantity takeoff workflows while establishing a modern foundation for AI-powered construction document intelligence.

### Reason

I am requesting an independent, open-source reimplementation of Bluebeam Revu that preserves its professional construction PDF workflows while introducing a modern, automation-first architecture with native AI, MCP integration, and intelligent quantity takeoff capabilities.

Bluebeam is valuable because it combines PDF document management, calibrated measurements, construction markups, drawing comparison, and quantity calculations in one specialized application.

However, there is an opportunity to create a more open, extensible, cross-platform alternative that allows users and AI agents to interact directly with construction documents and structured measurement data.

The objective is not simply to build another PDF editor. It is to create a professional construction document intelligence and estimating platform.

### 1. Native MCP server and Codex integration — foundational requirement

The application should provide a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server or first-party MCP adapter connected to a documented application API.

This would allow OpenAI Codex and other compatible AI agents to inspect, measure, annotate, compare, and analyze construction drawings directly.

Desired capabilities include:

- Open and inspect construction PDF sets.
- Identify drawing sheets, titles, and disciplines.
- Read drawing dimensions and annotations.
- Extract PDF vector geometry.
- Calibrate drawing scales.
- Create and edit measurement markups.
- Measure lengths, areas, perimeters, and counts.
- Identify doors, windows, fixtures, and building components.
- Generate quantity takeoffs.
- Compare drawing revisions.
- Create and modify PDF annotations.
- Extract and update markup data.
- Generate measurement and estimating reports.
- Export quantities to structured data formats.
- Run automated multi-sheet document workflows.

AI agents should operate on actual document geometry and structured measurement objects rather than relying on simulated mouse clicks.

### 2. Full scripting and automation API

The application should expose its core PDF, measurement, and markup functionality through a documented API.

Preferred capabilities:

- Python SDK.
- Structured JSON commands.
- Local API endpoints.
- Plugin and extension architecture.
- Batch processing.
- Event notifications.
- Background processing jobs.
- Structured error reporting.
- Reproducible measurement operations.
- Transactional edits with undo/redo.

The graphical interface, scripting API, and MCP server should share the same underlying measurement and document engines.

### 3. AI-powered construction quantity takeoffs

This should be one of the most important capabilities beyond conventional Bluebeam functionality.

The application should support intelligent interpretation of architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and civil drawings.

Potential capabilities include:

**Architectural**
- Wall lengths and areas.
- Door and window counts.
- Flooring areas.
- Ceiling areas.
- Drywall quantities.
- Painting areas.
- Baseboard and trim lengths.
- Roofing areas.

**Structural**
- Concrete areas and volumes.
- Footing and foundation measurements.
- Structural member counts.
- Framing quantities.
- Slab measurements.

**Mechanical and electrical**
- Equipment and fixture counts.
- Lighting fixture quantities.
- Plumbing fixture counts.
- Duct and pipe measurements.
- Electrical device counts.

**Civil and site**
- Site area measurements.
- Paving quantities.
- Curbs and sidewalks.
- Earthwork measurement inputs.
- Landscape area quantities.

AI should identify candidate objects and measurement regions, but final quantities must be calculated using calibrated geometry and verified rules.

The system should clearly distinguish detected objects, inferred quantities, and user-verified measurements.

### 4. AI drawing interpretation and document intelligence

The application should understand the relationships between construction drawings rather than treat every page as an unrelated image.

Desired capabilities:

- Automatic sheet classification.
- Drawing title and number extraction.
- Drawing index generation.
- Detection of drawing scales.
- Room and space identification.
- Dimension recognition.
- Door and window schedule extraction.
- Material specification extraction.
- Cross-referencing between plans, elevations, sections, and details.
- Identification of drawing inconsistencies.
- Detection of missing or conflicting information.
- Automated drawing summaries.

For example, an AI agent should be able to identify a door on a floor plan, locate its corresponding schedule entry, and retrieve its specified size, type, and hardware information.

Every extracted value should retain a reference to the source drawing and location.

### 5. Intelligent estimating and cost calculations

The application should extend quantity takeoffs into practical construction estimating.

Desired features:

- Custom material price databases.
- Labour rate tables.
- Labour productivity assumptions.
- Construction assemblies and cost formulas.
- Waste and overage factors.
- Equipment and subcontractor costs.
- Overhead and profit calculations.
- Tax and contingency settings.
- Trade-specific estimating templates.
- Regional pricing databases through optional integrations.
- Estimate revisions and comparisons.
- Export to Excel, CSV, and PDF.

Example workflow:

1. Import a residential construction drawing set.
2. Calibrate drawing scales.
3. Automatically identify walls, rooms, doors, and windows.
4. Generate preliminary quantity takeoffs.
5. Review and correct detected quantities.
6. Apply material and labour rates.
7. Calculate waste, overhead, and profit.
8. Generate an editable construction estimate.

All estimates should expose their assumptions, measurement sources, formulas, and confidence levels.

### 6. AI-assisted drawing revision comparison

Construction drawing revisions can introduce significant scope changes.

The application should support:

- Automatic alignment of revised drawings.
- Detection of added and removed building elements.
- Comparison of dimension changes.
- Identification of changed notes and specifications.
- Quantity changes between revisions.
- Highlighting of affected drawing areas.
- Revision-based estimate adjustments.
- Exportable change reports.

Example:

A revised floor plan moves several walls and adds two windows.

The application identifies the changed geometry, updates the relevant quantities, and highlights potential cost impacts for user review.

### 7. Construction document search and cross-referencing

The application should provide intelligent search across entire drawing sets.

Users should be able to search for:

- Room names.
- Door and window identifiers.
- Materials.
- Equipment tags.
- Drawing notes.
- Specifications.
- Detail references.
- Construction assemblies.
- Dimensions and measurements.

Results should link directly to the relevant drawing sheet and location.

AI-powered semantic search could supplement traditional text search, but should not replace reliable PDF text extraction and indexing.

### 8. Local-first architecture and privacy

Construction documents frequently contain confidential project information.

The application should support:

- Local document storage.
- Offline PDF viewing and markup.
- Offline calibrated measurements.
- Local quantity calculations.
- Local OCR where supported.
- Optional local AI models.
- User-controlled cloud processing.
- No mandatory cloud subscription for core functionality.
- Clear permission controls for external AI services.
- Explicit approval before uploading project documents to cloud providers.

### 9. Optional AI model and API integrations

Advanced AI drawing interpretation could use local models or external AI APIs.

The architecture should support:

- Local computer vision models.
- Document OCR and layout recognition.
- Multimodal vision-language models.
- Unified AI API providers such as PoYo where appropriate.
- Specialized document-processing services.
- User-supplied API credentials.
- Pay-as-you-go processing.
- Per-job cost estimates and spending limits.

The underlying measurement engine should remain deterministic and independent of generative AI providers.

### 10. Professional user interface

The application should provide a polished, efficient desktop interface designed for professional estimators and construction document reviewers.

Suggested workspace:

**Central drawing viewport**
- Large, high-performance PDF viewer.
- Smooth zoom and pan.
- Multiple document tabs.
- Split-screen comparison.
- Calibrated measurement overlays.

**Left sidebar**
- Drawing sheets.
- Bookmarks.
- Layers.
- Document navigation.
- Search results.

**Right sidebar**
- Measurement tools.
- Markup properties.
- Tool libraries.
- AI-assisted detection.
- Object and quantity inspection.

**Bottom panel**
- Structured markup list.
- Quantity takeoff table.
- Custom calculation columns.
- Cost and estimate summaries.
- Filters and grouping.

The interface should support professional dark mode without excessive visual effects, clutter, or chatbot-style workflows.

AI features should be integrated naturally into measurement, markup, and estimating tools.

### 11. Suggested technical architecture

The application should use a modular architecture.

**PDF document engine**
- Vector and raster PDF rendering.
- Text extraction.
- OCR.
- Annotation editing.
- Document organization.

**Measurement engine**
- Coordinate systems.
- Scale calibration.
- Geometric measurements.
- Units and precision.
- Measurement validation.

**Markup and takeoff engine**
- Structured markup objects.
- Quantity calculations.
- Classification and grouping.
- Custom formulas.
- Reporting.

**Document intelligence engine**
- Drawing classification.
- Object detection.
- Schedule extraction.
- Cross-sheet references.
- Revision comparison.

**Estimating engine**
- Material and labour pricing.
- Assembly calculations.
- Waste factors.
- Overhead and profit.
- Estimate reporting.

**Automation engine**
- Public application API.
- Python SDK.
- Native MCP server.
- Plugin architecture.
- Background jobs.

**Collaboration engine**
- Shared projects.
- Comments and review states.
- Revision history.
- Access permissions.

Existing mature, legally compatible PDF libraries should be evaluated rather than developing a PDF rendering engine from scratch.

### 12. Suggested development phases

**Phase 1 — Professional PDF foundation**

Implement PDF rendering, document navigation, markup tools, calibrated measurements, and a structured markup database.

Establish the application API and automation interfaces from the beginning.

**Phase 2 — Quantity takeoff workflows**

Implement measurement categories, counting tools, quantity summaries, custom formulas, tool sets, and spreadsheet exports.

**Phase 3 — Document comparison and batch processing**

Add drawing overlays, revision comparison, OCR, hyperlinks, batch operations, and document indexing.

**Phase 4 — Native MCP and scripting**

Expand the foundational API into a comprehensive MCP toolset supporting Codex-driven document inspection, measurement, annotation, and takeoff workflows.

**Phase 5 — AI drawing interpretation**

Add automatic object recognition, drawing classification, schedule extraction, cross-sheet analysis, and AI-assisted quantity takeoffs.

**Phase 6 — Estimating and collaboration**

Add material and labour pricing, construction assemblies, estimate generation, shared reviews, permissions, and advanced integrations.

### 13. Definition of success

A successful implementation should allow users to:

- Open and navigate large construction PDF sets.
- Accurately calibrate drawing scales.
- Perform professional measurements and markups.
- Generate structured construction quantity takeoffs.
- Compare drawing revisions.
- Manage reusable measurement tools.
- Export quantities and reports.
- Automate document workflows using Python.
- Allow Codex and other AI agents to inspect and modify drawings through MCP.
- Identify construction objects and generate AI-assisted preliminary takeoffs.
- Calculate construction estimates from verified quantities.
- Work locally without mandatory cloud subscriptions for core functionality.

The ultimate goal is a professional, open-source construction PDF, quantity takeoff, and estimating application that reproduces the most valuable Bluebeam Revu workflows while introducing modern automation, AI document intelligence, and extensible programmatic control.

All code and assets should be independently developed or obtained through legally compatible open-source licenses. The project should not copy proprietary Bluebeam source code, licensed assets, or protected branding.

### Official software URL

https://www.bluebeam.com/

General-purpose 3D CAD modeler based on NURBS geometry. Creates, edits,

### Original software

Toon Boom Harmony

### What the software does

Toon Boom Harmony is a professional 2D animation production software used for traditional frame-by-frame animation, digital drawing, character rigging, cut-out animation, compositing, and visual effects.

I would like to see a fully open-source reimplementation that provides a professional animation workflow comparable to Toon Boom Harmony.

**Key features to reproduce:**

- Professional vector and bitmap drawing engines.
- Frame-by-frame traditional 2D animation.
- Advanced timeline and exposure sheet (X-sheet).
- Onion skinning and drawing substitution.
- Advanced character rigging and bone systems.
- Deformers, mesh deformation, and master controllers.
- Node-based compositing and visual effects.
- Professional brushes, pencils, and painting tools.
- 2D camera system with multiplane and 3D camera movement.
- Audio synchronization and lip-sync animation.
- Scene management and reusable animation templates.
- High-quality rendering and export to MP4, GIF, PNG sequences, and other formats.
- Plugin and scripting API.
- Collaborative animation production and optional network-based project management.

The goal is to create an independent, modern, cross-platform, professional-grade 2D animation application.

### Reason

Toon Boom Harmony is an excellent professional animation tool, but its commercial licensing can make it difficult for independent animators, students, hobbyists, and small animation studios to access its complete workflow.

Existing open-source animation applications provide useful capabilities, but I would like to see a more comprehensive solution that combines traditional frame-by-frame animation, advanced character rigging, professional drawing tools, node-based compositing, and a production-ready timeline in one application.

A faithful open-source reimplementation would:

- Make professional 2D animation accessible to everyone.
- Provide a free alternative for independent animators and studios.
- Support both traditional and cut-out animation workflows.
- Allow developers to extend the software through plugins and scripting.
- Encourage community contributions and long-term development.
- Support collaborative animation projects and network-based workflows.

**Important:** This should be an independent implementation, without copying Toon Boom's proprietary source code, assets, or trademarks.

I believe this project could become an important open-source alternative to professional 2D animation software.

### Official software URL

https://www.toonboom.com/products/harmony

### Original software

Synology DSM (DiskStation Manager)

### What the software does

Synology DSM (DiskStation Manager) is the operating system that runs on Synology NAS boxes. It’s Linux underneath, but you manage it through a web browser that looks like a desktop.

What it does:

Storage management: sets up the drives into RAID/SHR volumes, monitors disk health, and handles snapshots so you can roll files back.
File sharing: shares folders over the network (SMB for Windows/Linux, NFS, AFP, FTP) and gives remote access through QuickConnect or your own domain.
Users and permissions: controls who can see and edit which folders.
Backup: Hyper Backup, Active Backup and Snapshot Replication back up the NAS itself, or back up PCs and servers to the NAS.
Apps (Package Center): installs extra services such as MailPlus (email server), Synology Photos, Drive (a Dropbox-style sync), Surveillance Station (cameras), Container Manager (Docker), and Virtual Machine Manager.
Security and maintenance: firewall, 2FA, automatic updates, and alerts by email or push when something fails.

In short, DSM turns a box of hard drives into a home or office server you can run from a browser, without needing to know Linux. MailPlus, which you use for email, is one of the apps running on top of it.

### Reason

The case for an open-source DSM-style project

The gap: DSM’s biggest selling point is its interface. It looks and feels like a desktop in the browser, with windows, a taskbar, app icons and a clean control panel. A non-technical person can set up shares, backups and users without touching a command line.

The open-source alternatives are powerful, but none of them match it:

TrueNAS: very capable, but the UI is technical and aimed at admins.
OpenMediaVault: functional, but dated and clunky.
Unraid: a decent UI, but it’s paid and not fully open source.
Proxmox: great for VMs, but it isn’t a NAS interface at all.

Why build it:

A DSM-quality interface: polished, desktop-style and beginner-friendly, which no open-source NAS currently offers.
No vendor lock-in: DSM only runs on Synology hardware, and Synology has been restricting drive compatibility. This would run on any PC, server or NAS box, with any drives.
Older model support: Synology drops updates for older models, leaving them stuck on outdated, insecure DSM versions. This project could give those boxes, and old PCs, a second life with ongoing updates instead of sending them to landfill.
Fully open source: it can be audited and maintained by the community, with no forced end-of-life.
A modern app ecosystem: built on Docker, so “apps” are just containers with a nice front end.
Lighter and modular: install only what you need, such as storage, shares, backup and Docker, and skip the bloat.
Better integration: it would fit into existing setups like Proxmox and Docker instead of forcing a closed app ecosystem.

### Official software URL

https://www.synology.com/en-au/support/download

### Original software

ProPresenter by Renewed Vision

### What the software does

ProPresenter is a professional church presentation and live production application designed to manage the visual and media aspects of church services, worship sessions, conferences, and other live events.

It provides a centralized production environment for controlling presentations, song lyrics, Bible scriptures, images, videos, audio playback, stage displays, and live-streaming outputs.

Its main capabilities include:

Presentation management: Create, organize, and control presentation slides, announcements, sermon notes, and service sequences.

Worship and lyrics management: Manage worship songs, lyrics, verses, choruses, transitions, and song libraries.

Bible integration: Search and display Bible passages across different translations, with automatic verse formatting and presentation controls.

Media playback: Play videos, audio tracks, background loops, images, and other media assets during live services.

Audio control: Manage audio playback, sound levels, audio routing, and media transitions.

Live video integration: Work with cameras, video sources, capture devices, and external production equipment.

Live streaming: Provide presentation and media outputs that can be integrated into streaming production workflows.

Multi-screen output: Independently control the main congregation display, stage display, confidence monitors, and additional presentation outputs.

Stage display: Show worship leaders, pastors, and production teams relevant information, including lyrics, notes, timers, and upcoming content.

Service planning: Arrange songs, scripture readings, announcements, videos, and sermon presentations into an organized service workflow.

Remote control: Allow authorized operators to control presentations and production remotely.

### Reason

I would like to see an independently developed, open-source alternative that reproduces the professional production capabilities of software like ProPresenter without being limited to basic slide presentations.

Many existing open-source presentation applications focus primarily on displaying slides, lyrics, or Bible verses. However, church production requires a much more integrated environment where presentations, worship lyrics, audio, video, media playback, stage displays, and streaming workflows can be controlled together.

The reimplementation should prioritize:

Unified production control: A centralized interface for managing every aspect of a live church service, rather than switching between multiple disconnected applications.

Real-time media control: Reliable audio and video playback, media transitions, background loops, and independent output management.

Advanced display management: Support for multiple independent displays, including congregation screens, stage monitors, confidence displays, and external video outputs.

Professional streaming workflows: Integration with OBS Studio, RTMP streaming destinations, NDI-compatible workflows, and external production systems.

Flexible service planning: Build reusable service plans, schedule presentation sequences, manage song libraries, and prepare entire services before they begin.

Reliable live operation: Low-latency controls, predictable transitions, offline operation, recovery from playback failures, and stable performance during live events.

Extensible architecture: Plugin support, integrations, media connectors, and APIs that allow churches to extend the production environment.

The goal is not simply to create another church slideshow application, but to independently reimplement a complete church presentation and live production environment that can serve small congregations as well as large churches with dedicated media and production teams.

The implementation should preserve the important workflows and capabilities of the original software while using an independently developed architecture, interface, and codebase.

### Official software URL

https://renewedvision.com/propresenter/
